comment: Default behaviour: output is in the order records appear in the smiles
file, NOT the order of the identifier file. data/ids.txt is deliberately
in a different order (ethanol, methane, benzene, propane) so that this
is distinguishable from the identifier-order mode in subset_S_order.
test.name: default

comment: -C selects the identifier column in the smiles file.
test.name: column_C3

comment: -I declares the column separator in the smiles file. Because a separator
was given, the tabs in the file are significant and are NOT translated to
spaces, so the records are echoed with their tabs intact.
Contrast with separator_I_tab_default below.
test.name: separator_II_tab

comment: A tab separated smiles file works with no -I at all: when no separator
has been declared the reader translates tabs to spaces. Note the output
records therefore contain spaces, not the original tabs.
This is long standing behaviour and must not change.
test.name: separator_II_tab_default

comment: -i declares the column separator in the identifier file.
test.name: separator_i_tab

comment: A tab separated identifier file with no -i. Tabs are translated to spaces
so this works. Previously the identifier reader did not translate tabs and
this case silently wrote nothing while still exiting 0.
test.name: separator_i_tab_default

comment: -d reports duplicate identifiers in the identifier file but continues.
test.name: duplicate_ids_d

comment: -q ignores duplicate identifiers silently.
test.name: duplicate_ids_q

comment: Without -d or -q a duplicate identifier in the identifier file is fatal.
Exits 6 and writes nothing.
test.name: duplicate_ids_fail

comment: By default only the first occurrence of an identifier in the smiles file
is written, even though haystack_dup.smi holds three records named methane.
test.name: first_instance_only

comment: -a writes every occurrence of an identifier in the smiles file.
test.name: all_instances_a

comment: -x inverts the selection: writes the records NOT requested.
test.name: invert_x

comment: -z strips leading zeros so 000123 matches 123.
test.name: strip_zeros_z

comment: -j skips the header record of a descriptor-style identifier file.
Note the remaining descriptor column is appended to each output record.
test.name: descriptor_header_j

comment: By default any extra columns from the identifier file are appended
to the output record.
test.name: annotate_default

comment: -k suppresses the extra information from the identifier file.
test.name: suppress_info_k

comment: -n sets the string placed before the identifier file information.
test.name: info_separator_n

comment: -K names identifiers on the command line INSTEAD of reading an identifier
file, so only the smiles file is passed. Supplying an identifier file as
well makes that file be treated as the haystack.
test.name: explicit_ids_K

comment: -X collects smiles records that were not requested; -Y collects requested
identifiers absent from the smiles file.
Uses a shell script because the -Y file is produced by iterating a hash,
so its order is not guaranteed and must be sorted before comparison.
Note the other_commands field of the test proto is NOT implemented by
run_all_test.rb, so a shell script is the only way to post-process.
test.name: unmatched_X_Y

comment: -w writes the -Y file as a smiles file, appending .smi to the name.
Sorted before comparison for the same reason as unmatched_X_Y.
test.name: unmatched_Y_smiles_w

comment: -C RX= makes the identifier whichever column matches the regexp.
Only methane matches ^meth among the requested identifiers; methanol
matches the regexp but was never requested.
test.name: regexp_C_RX

comment: THE IDENTIFIER-ORDER MODE. -S hashes the smiles file and streams the
identifier file, so output follows identifier-file order
(ethanol, methane, benzene, propane) rather than smiles-file order.
This is the same behaviour the separate fetch_smiles tool provides.
-S formerly returned exit code 1 on success. It now returns 0, matching
the rest of the tool.
test.name: subset_S_order

comment: -g sets the starting index for the files created by -S.
test.name: subset_S_g1

comment: With -S every leading file is an identifier file and the last is the
haystack, producing one subset per identifier file.
test.name: subset_S_multiple
